findings.reason: either a node must wire the four counts into the composed brief/prompt (or the reviewer cannot name them), or §3's second done-when is unmeetable and should be cut.
findings.text: §3's "Also done when" requires the review of a plan to name the current week's four interface counts from `reckon/interface_counts.py`, but that module is referenced nowhere in the composer (`reckon/crew/recovery.py`) or the design-review prompt, so the clause has no mechanism behind it

findings.reason: §10's deliverable and done-when name "`_is_review_node` and `_is_review_run`" but there are two `_is_review_run` readers and §10 frames the defect as a duplicated literal, not this behavioural divergence; §10 must name both readers and require both prefixes recognised.
findings.text: dispatch's `_is_review_run` recognises only `REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX` ("review-of-"), while `reckon/crew/recovery.py:238` `_is_review_node` also accepts the bare "plan-review-of-", so a plan-review node is classified as a plain node by `_task_identity` (dispatch.py:11238) and takes a different session identity than recovery expects

findings.reason: §9 already established that the shared report grammar belongs in `review.py`; PR-1 could extend that store layer or state in the plan why the plan+version+fingerprint key forces a fork, so the two selection implementations cannot drift.
findings.text: the plan adds a second versioned record store (`store_plan_review`/`read_plan_review`/`_candidate_paths`/`_target_path`/`_stored_blob8`) parallel to `reckon/crew/review.py`'s (`store_review`/`read_review`/`_partial_review_path`/`_complete_review_exists`/`_stored_partial_identity`) under the same `review_store_root`, duplicating the path, revision-sibling and newest-by-mtime selection logic that file already owns

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` hides the record shape, the content fingerprint, the store and the report→record join behind a small, coherent interface, and the dispatch composer is shared (`plan_review_subject` feeds the same `_review_dispatch_fields`) rather than forked.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `plan_review.py` re-implements the versioned-record store that `reckon/crew/review.py` owns, and `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`'s `_is_review_run` forks the review-node predicate recovery.py already defines.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites `reckon/interface_counts.py` as the interface-budget source in §3, but no mechanism (composer or prompt) reuses it, so the citation is not carried into the design.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — each layer the plan adds states why it cannot be an extension: the shared composer per D6, the shared report parser per §9, and one constant per §10; no unjustified wrapper was found beyond the store fork reported below.
